identity_evidence: The visually verified NARA row supplies Ira Ashley, Second Lieutenant, a private Army identifier, and Box 24. An eyewitness account by Egon Larsen explicitly identifies Second Lieutenant Ira Ashley as an OSS contact in London in April 1944. Contemporary Broadcasting notices independently identify Private Ira Ashley in Army basic training at Keesler Field in October 1943 and Ira Ashley returning from OSS duties in London in December 1945. The exact name, matching rank, direct OSS link, London location, and continuous military chronology confirm the identity.
research_status_message: Review Box 24 and Army records to establish Ira Ashley's enlistment and commissioning dates, exact Keesler assignment, OSS entry order, and whether his 1943 Stage Door Canteen production work had a named employing organization. Lambert & Feasley is the last named civilian employer currently documented, not necessarily the final civilian engagement.
next_action: Review Box 24 and Army records to establish Ira Ashley's enlistment and commissioning dates, exact Keesler assignment, OSS entry order, and whether his 1943 Stage Door Canteen production work had a named employing organization. Lambert & Feasley is the last named civilian employer currently documented, not necessarily the final civilian engagement.

immediate_pre_oss_affiliations.date_precision: Contemporary reporting places Private Ashley in basic training at Keesler Field on October 4, 1943; an eyewitness places Second Lieutenant Ashley with OSS in London in April 1944. Exact entry, commissioning, transfer, and unit dates are unknown.

last_civilian_pre_service.date_precision: A contemporary October 1942 trade notice states that Ashley would resign November 1 after three years with the agency.

other_pre_oss_affiliations.date_precision: A contemporary October 4, 1943 notice identifies Ashley as producer of the program while reporting that he was then in Army basic training; exact production dates and employer are not supplied.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Second Lieutenant Ira Ashley is confirmed as the New York radio producer who served with OSS in London.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Our 'contact' with the top people was 2nd Lieutenant Ira Ashley.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA rank and exact name match an eyewitness OSS London account, while contemporary trade reporting independently links the same exact name to Army training and OSS London duties.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the uncommon exact name, matching Second Lieutenant rank, direct eyewitness OSS identification, London location, and continuous contemporary military-service chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish Army training in October 1943, OSS contact duties in London by April 1944, and return from OSS London duties in 1945.
claims.match_notes: No claim relies on the private service identifier. The rank and direct OSS chronology independently bridge the public evidence to the indexed person.
